Drafts: a Broke vs Smart flip-math post using the 65% all-in rule, a seller-POV twist, and a bricks + Bitcoin debate question.

drafts.draft_en:
Same Philly rowhome. ARV $250K. Needs $50K in work.

Broke flipper:
Pays $190K
All in: $240K (96% of ARV)
Profit after costs: hope

Smart flipper:
Caps purchase + repairs at 65% of ARV
All in: $162.5K
Max offer: $112.5K

The money is made when you buy.
drafts.pattern: Broke vs Smart side-by-side (@shaguncrypto credit-card format). Uses Bar's flip rule correctly: purchase plus repairs, all in, at or under 65% of ARV, for flips only. Hypothetical numbers, no promised returns.
drafts.video_tip: 12–15s whiteboard split screen: left column 'Broke', right 'Smart'. Write the numbers live, circle $112.5K at the end. Burn in captions; pin a reply asking 'What's your max %?'

drafts.draft_en:
POV: The seller says, "Nobody's going to buy this house the way it is."

So you don't ask them to fix it.

You make a fair as-is offer, cover the closing costs, and let them pick the date.

Inherited, behind on repairs, tired of the stress? That's a conversation, not a dead end.
drafts.pattern: 'They said X. So I did Y.' twist (@EllasArchive1, high save rate), framed as POV so it isn't a made-up personal story. Ties to @workwithbar's Philly as-is seller offer.
drafts.video_tip: 8–10s: walk up to a beat-up rowhome door, on-screen text with the seller's line, cut to a handshake or keys. Captions on. CTA in the pinned reply, not the post.

drafts.draft_en:
Grant Cardone's fund just added Bitcoin to a real estate project.

Bricks + BTC in the same deal.

Smart hedge, or stacking two kinds of risk?

I want real reasons in the replies.
